candidates.name: g0v/tw-rental-house-data
candidates.what_it_holds: MIT-licensed civic-tech (g0v) pipeline collecting publicly available Taiwan long-term rental listing data (rental websites + branded apartment operators). Four sub-components: scrapy-tw-rental-house (Scrapy scraper, DB-independent), twrh-dataset (full scrape->store->export->publish pipeline), csv-aggregator (dedupes and rolls monthly captures into quarterly/yearly CSVs), ui-next (web UI at rentalhouse.g0v.ddio.io). 713 commits, 174 stars, 45 watchers, 36 forks, 11 open issues -- actively maintained. Also published as a PyPI package.
candidates.why_useful: Non-Airbnb long-term-rental data source and a working, non-trivial scraper/pipeline for an APAC market (gap #13: LTR/housing crossover data, and gap #7 APAC regional coverage). Could be adapted as a template for STR<->LTR crossover economics or as a live check on Taiwan rent trends feeding into host-supply economics.
candidates.time_coverage: Ongoing scrape, aggregated to monthly/quarterly/yearly; exact start date not stated in README summary
candidates.size_hint: Multi-repo pipeline, 713 commits; dataset size not stated (published via PyPI + web UI, not a single flat file)
candidates.last_activity: Active as of search (174 stars/45 watchers/36 forks, open issues/PRs)

candidates.name: thomasthinks/poland-rent-data
candidates.what_it_holds: Nightly-updated Polish long-term rental market medians: a current-snapshot CSV (470 rows, city x district x room-count combinations with median rent in PLN, dispersion stat, sample size, snapshot date), a JSON version with provenance metadata, and a CSV history file of monthly city-level trends. Aggregates and deduplicates listings across three portals (Otodom, OLX, Morizon) across all 16 Polish voivodeships, 49 cities, 96 districts, 1-4 room flats. CC-BY-4.0, archived with a Zenodo DOI (10.5281/zenodo.21892638).
candidates.why_useful: A committed, licensed, cross-source-deduplicated asking-rent nowcast dataset for an EU market not otherwise in the held set (gap #13: Idealista/Rightmove/Immoscout-style EU rent scrapes) -- could proxy EU housing-cost/consumer-strength pressure feeding into EMEA nights/ADR context.
candidates.time_coverage: Monthly history from approx. June 2026; current snapshot dated 13 Sep 2026; history is forward-only (cannot be backfilled)
candidates.size_hint: 470-row current snapshot; monthly history file since mid-2026; small, no visible star count

candidates.name: pranaavdhakshesh/ETL-Housing-Pipeline
candidates.what_it_holds: ETL pipeline and REST API for US housing affordability by zip code, with committed CSV files already merging three public sources: acs_income_data_2022.csv / acs_income_info.csv (Census ACS), hud_county_data.csv / hud_rent_info.csv (HUD Fair Market Rent), and zip_info.csv/county_info.csv/state_info.csv (Zillow + geography crosswalks). Code loads these static files rather than re-pulling at runtime. 3 commits total; no explicit license found.
candidates.why_useful: One of very few repos that actually commits merged Zillow + HUD FMR + Census files (zip/county/state level) rather than just code pointing at the source portals -- saves the crosswalk/merge work for a host-supply-economics or affordability-vs-STR-supply cut (gap #13).
candidates.size_hint: 7 committed CSV files; 3 commits total, small repo

candidates.name: panasenco/rentmap
candidates.what_it_holds: Python visualization tool (rentmap.py) that maps Zillow Observed Rent Index (ZORI) at the zip-code level -- user must download the ZORI file from Zillow Research and drop it in /data; also overlays unrelated civic datasets (midwifery friendliness, political affiliation, vaccine/homeschool law, Colorado crime, climate/mosquito data). 8 commits, actively touched as recently as Aug 2026, no explicit license, uses git submodules.
candidates.why_useful: Confirms Zillow ZORI zip-level download path and gives ready mapping/visualization code, but holds no committed rent data itself -- a thin acquisition-method wrapper, not a dataset.
candidates.time_coverage: Whatever vintage of ZORI the user supplies
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Zillow ZORI itself is a well-known public series (not previously catalogued by name in our holdings, but this repo adds no data beyond the raw Zillow download)

candidates.name: VestMap-App
candidates.what_it_holds: Org profile page for a commercial CRE/real-estate data product (VestMap) that says it packages demographics, population, household income, median rent, home values, crime indexes, employment, growth projections and FEMA flood risk, sourced from ESRI, AGS, FHFA HPI, FEMA NRI and US Census. No data files in the GitHub org itself; points to a commercial app/product.
candidates.why_useful: Marginal -- names FHFA HPI and median-rent as inputs to a commercial product, useful only as a pointer to what upstream public sources (FHFA HPI, Census) exist; the org holds no data itself.
candidates.size_hint: N/A -- org profile page only, no data repo
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: FHFA HPI / Census are standard public sources already implicitly accessible; no new data added

WebFetch verification of g0v/tw-rental-house-data, thomasthinks/poland-rent-data, pranaavdhakshesh/ETL-Housing-Pipeline, panasenco/rentmap, VaishnaviMane17 repo
notes: Both primary modalities this scout was told to try (WebSearch, and DuckDuckGo HTML fallback) failed structurally: WebSearch's session-wide budget (shared across the whole ~200-scout sweep) was reported exhausted before I made a single call, and html.duckduckgo.com refused the connection outright. Bing via WebFetch loaded but its small-model page summary did not surface github.com links for these queries even though ~468k raw results existed per the page text -- likely lost in JS-rendering/truncation. `gh search repos` (CLI) hit the account's GitHub API rate limit after only 4 calls; the required "sleep 40s and retry once" could not be executed because this harness's anti-sleep guard blocks bare Bash/PowerShell sleeps (I used the Monitor tool as a workaround for the wait, then found `gh` still 403'd, so I pivoted). The one channel that worked reliably was direct WebFetch against the unauthenticated `https://api.github.com/search/repositories?q=...` JSON endpoint -- this is effectively "web search" against GitHub's own index and is what most of this catalogue is built from. Substantive finding for the theme itself: there is no GitHub repo replicating or hosting a new-tenant/repeat-rent index (Cleveland Fed style) or a shelter-CPI nowcast model -- multiple targeted queries returned zero hits. The Zillow ZORI / Apartment List space on GitHub is entirely populated by disposable student ML-notebook projects that pull the official Zillow Research CSV at runtime and do a regression/clustering exercise on it (excluded per instructions as boilerplate re-analysis with no new data) -- e.g. VaishnaviMane17/Real-Estate-Market-Analysis-Using-CAPM- (511 metros, ZORI 2015-2023 + ZHVI 2000-2023, but data pulled live via FRED API, nothing committed) was checked and excluded on this basis. The few repos worth flagging are long-term-rental data pipelines for non-US markets (Taiwan, Poland) and one small ETL repo that pre-merges Zillow+HUD+Census into committed CSVs. Suggest a future scout hit this specific gap via Zenodo/OSF/SSRN-linked academic replication packages or the BLS/Cleveland Fed/San Francisco Fed GitHub orgs directly rather than generic keyword search, since the underlying methodology (NTRR, shelter CPI decomposition) lives in agency working papers, not community repos.
